No restore point could be created because System Protection is off on drive {surucu}.

Turn it on? This will:
• Turn on System Protection for drive {surucu}
• Reserve up to {gb} GB for restore points (free space: {bos} GB; the oldest points are deleted as it fills)
• Create the first restore point and check that it really exists

To turn it off later: Control Panel > System > System protection > Configure.

ui.wu.aciklama.varsayilan: Leaves Windows Update to Windows' own settings. If the app applied a mode before, the previous values are restored.
ui.wu.aciklama.guvenlik: Feature (major version) updates are deferred 365 days and quality updates 4 days; drivers do not come from Windows Update; updates are downloaded but you are asked before they install. Same values as Chris Titus Tech WinUtil's 'Security Settings'.
ui.wu.aciklama.duraklat: Extends Windows' 'Pause updates' setting until 1 January 2100. During this time security updates do NOT arrive either. No service is disabled and no file is deleted; undo it with 'Default'.
ui.wu.arti.guvenlik: Security patches arrive within a few days; no surprise major versions or drivers
ui.wu.arti.duraklat: No update downloads or unexpected restarts while gaming
ui.wu.eksi.guvenlik: New Windows features arrive a year late; you have to update drivers such as the graphics driver yourself
ui.wu.eksi.duraklat: Security holes stay open; some games, Microsoft Store and anti-cheat systems may require an up-to-date Windows
ui.wu.dokunmamali.guvenlik: Computers managed by a company or school
ui.wu.dokunmamali.duraklat: Anyone who browses the web, opens email or does online banking; managed computers
ui.wu.dikkat.guvenlik: Because policy values are written, Settings may say 'Some settings are managed by your organization'; this is normal.
ui.wu.dikkat.duraklat: This method relies on undocumented Windows values and was not tested on this computer; Windows may reset the limit itself in the future. Switch back to 'Default' from time to time and install updates.
ui.wu.not: Turning Windows Update off completely (disabling its services) is deliberately not offered: it is hard to undo and Windows often turns it back on by itself.

Extensions run inside the browser; they affect an open browser, not the game itself. If the browser stays open while you play, enabled extensions use memory and CPU. The effect is usually small and was not measured in this app; closing the browser before gaming is the surest way.

The "runs on all sites" mark means the extension can read and change every page. It is a privacy notice, not a slowness indicator.

The app does not change or delete extensions. The "Remove in browser" button only opens the browser's page for that extension (the general extensions page in Firefox); you remove it there yourself. Brave, Vivaldi and Opera have no button: type brave://extensions or similar in the address bar. The list is read only from files on this PC and never sent anywhere. Outside Chrome, this reading was not tested on a real computer.

ui.oyun_bilgi.hazir_ayar:
The three presets fill in this game's system-side settings with one click:

• Visual priority: does not push the system (priority Normal). With two graphics cards it sends the game to the powerful one.
• Balanced: priority Above Normal.
• Performance: priority High.

None of them changes the game's own graphics settings. These values are not a promised gain; they are a starting point. You can see the effect with the Before/After measurement.

ui.bilgi.amac: Forevermore is a Windows settings app for gamers. It scans your PC read-only and shows the settings that actually work, with what they do and their pros and cons; placebo and harmful settings are marked separately. Every change is backed up and can be undone with one click.
ui.bilgi.hikaye: I have been into computers and optimization as a hobby for a long time. Because there is so much fake news, misleading settings and baseless optimization online, I wanted to design a simple, easy-to-use app based on my own tests, benchmarks and experience. Forevermore is a university student's hobby project.

olcum.aciklama: Take a 'Before' measurement before applying settings and an 'After' measurement after applying them (and restarting if needed); the app compares the two. Results are stored on this computer only.
olcum.durustluk: Honest warning: a single measurement is not proof. Results vary with background activity, temperature and the scene. Under the same conditions (same scene, same duration, same open programs), take at least 3 measurements each and compare the averages. Small differences (below 3%) are often measurement noise.
olcum.sistem_aciklama: Boot time (from the event log), startup apps and tasks, services, idle CPU/memory and process count. Do not use the computer during the measurement; the most accurate result is a few minutes after the computer starts.

olcum.oyun_ipucu: Open the game and always go to the same scene (e.g. the same map, the same round). After 'Start measurement', go back to the game during the {sn}-second countdown; only time with the game in the foreground counts.
olcum.not_ac_tam_ekran: PresentMon does not inject into the game; it reads Windows event logs (ETW), so it is not expected to conflict with anti-cheat such as VAC (still, measure in practice mode, not an online match). In exclusive fullscreen, alt-tab minimises the game and the counter stops: borderless window is recommended.
